patch.value: History maintenance triplicates one load, verify, rewrite, re-anchor, report pipeline across redact, repair and compact instead of sharing a stream-maintenance primitive

The history subsystem is 5,807 lines across 18 files. Three of them are the maintenance operations and they are the three largest: src/sdk/history-redact.ts at 930 lines, src/sdk/history-compact.ts at 878, src/sdk/history-repair.ts at 728. Each performs the same pipeline — read the stream, verify the hash chain, apply a per-operation transform, re-anchor the chain, reconcile against the on-disk item, and emit a dry-run plan plus an applied report — and each implements that pipeline separately. A shared src/core/history/history-rewrite.ts exists at 226 lines but covers only part of it.

Measured with jscpd in strict mode at 12 lines and 60 tokens over src, packages and scripts (the repository gate runs at 22 lines and 115 tokens, which reports zero; that sensitivity gap is pm-xspd). Clone pairs inside this family:

  sdk/history-redact.ts:784   <-> sdk/history-repair.ts:452    22 lines, 95 tokens
  sdk/history-compact.ts:372  <-> sdk/history-repair.ts:400    16 lines, 92 tokens
  sdk/history-compact.ts:412  <-> sdk/history-read.ts:122      20 lines, 73 tokens
  cli/commands/copy.ts:110    <-> sdk/history-repair.ts:439    19 lines, 88 tokens
  cli/commands/restore.ts:144 <-> sdk/history-redact.ts:738    19 lines, 80 tokens
  cli/commands/copy.ts:110    <-> sdk/history-compact.ts:411   15 lines, 74 tokens
  cli/commands/copy.ts:110    <-> cli/commands/restore.ts:336  15 lines, 71 tokens

The last four matter beyond duplication: cli/commands/copy.ts and cli/commands/restore.ts are re-implementing stream handling that the SDK owns, which is the SDK-first inversion pm-usfg exists to remove.

The cost is not line count, it is that each maintenance operation can drift in how it verifies and re-anchors. That is the exact surface where a divergence is silent and unrecoverable: a rewriter that re-anchors slightly differently from its siblings produces a stream that verifies under one command and not another. It also multiplies the work of every future history invariant by three.

Consolidating is a simplification with zero capability change: the three commands keep their flags, output shapes and semantics, and differ only in the transform they hand to one shared maintenance primitive.

Scope boundary. pm-yh8r owns intra-file LOC decomposition as a general policy; pm-xspd owns the duplication-detection gate; pm-9yfo owns proving every mutation appends history; pm-klo8 owns the workspace-level stream. This is the specific consolidation of the item-stream maintenance pipeline that all of them assume exists.

One SDK primitive owns the load, verify, transform, re-anchor, reconcile and report pipeline for item history streams, and redact, repair and compact are expressed as transforms handed to it. cli/commands/copy.ts and cli/commands/restore.ts consume that primitive rather than re-implementing stream handling. The externally observable behaviour of every history command — flags, dry-run plans, applied reports, exit codes — is unchanged, asserted by the existing suites passing without modification. A jscpd run at 12 lines and 60 tokens reports no remaining clone pair inside the history family.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Scope input 2026-07-31 from pm-aka8m7. This chore consolidates the load, verify, rewrite, re-anchor, report pipeline across redact, repair and compact, and that consolidation is the right and only place to add one thing all three paths currently omit.

reanchorHistoryEntries at src/core/history/replay.ts:365-370 overwrites before_hash and after_hash in place and retains the prior values nowhere - the result carries an entriesRehashed count and a per-entry rehashed boolean. Every one of the three commands this chore unifies therefore destroys the anchors its inputs committed to, and so does every union merge, since src/sdk/merge/three-way.ts:57 documents reanchored as true for every union. Adding retention per command would mean writing it three times and would leave the merge driver's own path a fourth; adding it at the unified pipeline covers all four at once.

Recommend widening this chore's acceptance criteria to include the retention hook - the shared pipeline emits the original anchor pair for each rewritten entry to whichever durable sink the owning command chooses - without taking on the storage-location decision, which belongs to pm-aka8m7. That keeps this chore mechanical while making the fix a one-site change afterwards rather than a four-site one.
